speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I am Dr. Agent; you are presenting with fever, headache, anorexia, fatigue, and malaise. Are you currently pregnant, and if so, how many weeks along are you?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old female at 30 weeks gestation. The patient presents with a sudden onset of fever, headache, anorexia, fatigue, and malaise. She reports the consumption of ice cream 3 days prior to the onset of symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Since you are 30 weeks pregnant and consumed ice cream three days before your symptoms started, were you able to thoroughly wash your hands after handling the ice cream or eating it? Also, has anyone around you been diagnosed with a similar illness recently?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fever. I also have Headache, Anorexia, Fatigue, Malaise.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Listeriosis (Listeria monocytogenes infection)

The combination of sudden-onset fever, headache, and severe fatigue in a pregnant woman at 30 weeks, particularly following ingestion of potentially contaminated dairy products like ice cream, is highly suggestive of Listeriosis. This condition poses a significant risk for preterm labor and sepsis in the fetus.

I will now request specific laboratory results to confirm the diagnosis and determine the appropriate treatment.
